paper_metadata.title: Towards practical Quantum Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper presents a toy credit-risk experiment using iterative quantum amplitude estimation on a 2-asset, 2-risk-factor model, simulated on Qiskit’s qasm simulator. The reported setup uses 6 qubits in the loading circuit, target precision ε = 0.002, 99% confidence, and about 50,000 quantum samples; the paper claims a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo but does not demonstrate practical advantage on hardware.

experiments.description: Toy-model credit risk analysis using iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) on a multi-factor uncertainty model with multiple rotations, evaluated on a Qiskit simulator for a 2-asset, 2-risk-factor example with non-integer LGD values.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with multi-factor uncertainty model, multiple-rotations encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ε = 0.002 and 99% target confidence interval

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each asset default probability is encoded via Y-rotations controlled by discretized normal risk-factor registers; two qubits encode each latent normal variable Z1 and Z2, and asset default qubits are rotated according to the weighted sum of risk factors.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α by finding the smallest x such that P[L ≤ x] ≥ α, then compute Ecap = VaR_α - E[L].
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Bisection search over threshold x; objective qubit flipped when total loss is less than or equal to x.

problem_instance.description: Illustrative two-asset credit portfolio with two systemic risk factors and non-integer loss-given-default values.

dataset_specification.description: Table 1 parameters: asset 1 LGD=1000.5, p0=0.15, rho=0.1, weights (0.35, 0.2); asset 2 LGD=2000.5, p0=0.25, rho=0.05, weights (0.1, 0.25).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretized and truncated standard normal distributions for risk factors; affine mapping from discrete indices to normal values.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Classical simulation of the quantum circuit using Qiskit qasm simulator; iterative amplitude estimation with target precision and confidence; VaR estimated at α=0.95.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct multi-factor uncertainty circuit; discretize normal distributions; perform bisection search over VaR threshold.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use estimated cumulative distribution to identify VaR_0.95 and compute economic capital conceptually.

speedup_claims.conditions: credit risk analysis / value-at-risk estimation using amplitude estimation; IQAE variant avoids QPE and still maintains quadratic speedup
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed asymptotic advantage; no direct empirical runtime comparison on hardware. The paper notes real hardware noise destroys output.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo via amplitude estimation; IQAE avoids QPE and still provides quadratic speedup.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(√n) Monte Carlo convergence rate for n simulation paths.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 6 logical qubits for the toy circuit as shown in Figure 6, plus substantially more for realistic portfolios; the paper also notes the need for improved coherence and that real hardware noise destroys the output.
limiting_factors: No empirical comparison against a classical baseline runtime or accuracy on the same task
Paper explicitly states real quantum hardware noise destroys the output
Claimed speedup is quadratic amplitude-estimation speedup, which is not practically viable under Hoefler-style constant-factor overheads
Scalability concerns: circuit width and depth grow substantially with more assets and risk factors

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly states the experiment was run on the Qiskit qasm simulator back-end rather than a real QPU.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only qualitative scaling and qubit count are given.
50000 quantum samples are reported as the average number of samples used by IQAE.
The paper claims a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo for amplitude estimation, but only demonstrates a simulator-based toy example with 2 assets and 2 risk factors.
No hardware advantage is shown; the authors explicitly note that noise on real quantum architectures destroys the output.
